title: task-creation guide: warn that a count baked into an acceptance criterion goes stale while the task is open
description:
Found on this repository own QCLI-348 and generalised with opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-19. This repository SHIPS the guide that tells every agent in the fleet how to write acceptance criteria, and the guide does not cover this.

WHAT HAPPENED. QCLI-348 was filed with the criterion "The three daemons currently alive on this host are reaped once inspection is finished". Within the hour there were four: a fourth process started after the measurement was taken. Neither count was wrong -- both were accurate at their own instant -- but the criterion had a number in it, so it became unsatisfiable-as-written by something entirely outside the task scope. It was rewritten to enumerate at fix time.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is what belongs in the guide rather than the anecdote. A criterion is a promise about a future state, so a figure inside one is a claim that the figure will still hold when someone comes to check. That is safe for a count of things the task itself controls (files it will change, flags it will add) and unsafe for a count of anything the world produces -- live processes, open PRs, records in a directory, rows in a report. The failure is quiet: the criterion still reads as checkable, and whoever checks it either ticks it against a number that no longer means anything or gets stuck on a discrepancy that is not a defect.

opum-cli-e2e generalised the measurement half the same way and it is worth carrying alongside: a count of live things is a measurement with an instant attached and is meaningless without one. They cite two sessions reading a month-to-date billing figure minutes apart and getting different CORRECT answers, where the disagreement was the finding rather than an error in either read.

WHAT THE GUIDE SAYS TODAY. quest instructions task-creation says: "Write acceptance criteria as outcomes someone else could verify without asking you what you meant." That is right and does not cover this -- a criterion naming a count IS verifiable and IS unambiguous; it just stops being true. The addition is about durability, not clarity, which is why it does not fall out of the existing sentence.

NOT proposing validation or a lint. There is no way to tell a safe count from an unsafe one mechanically, and a rule that rejects digits in criteria would be worse than the problem. This is a sentence in the guide.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest instructions task-creation tells the author to write a criterion that enumerates at check time rather than baking in a count of anything the task does not itself control, and says why -- the criterion stops being true rather than becoming unclear.
The guidance distinguishes the safe case (a count of what the task will produce) from the unsafe one (a count of live or external state), so it does not read as a blanket ban on numbers.
The change is prose in the guide only: no new validation, no lint, and no rejection of criteria containing digits.
The guide contract test that pins recipe counts per guide still passes, or is updated deliberately in the same change if the recipe count moves.

plan: 1. Add a paragraph to the task-creation guide after the verifiable-outcomes sentence: enumerate at check time instead of baking in a count of live or external state; a count of what the task itself produces is fine; the failure is that the criterion stops being true, not that it becomes unclear.
2. Prose only, no fence, so EXPECTED_RECIPES task-creation stays 8; pin the new guidance with a test that reads the rendered guide.
3. bun run check; PR into dev closing the task.
implementationNotes: Evidence. The new paragraph sits in the task-creation guide in src/application/agents/guides.ts, straight after the verifiable-outcomes sentence. test/qcli351-criterion-count-durability.test.ts reads the rendered guide text and pins five things: the enumerate-at-check-time instruction, the no-longer-true reason, the safe case, the unsafe case, and "not numbers in general". It failed 0/1 with the guides.ts change stashed and passed with it. The change adds no fence, so EXPECTED_RECIPES task-creation stays 8, and test/contract/guide-commands.test.ts passed unchanged. There is no validation or lint, and no src change outside guide prose. bun run check: 855 pass, 0 fail.
